#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
"""The similarity audit (R-AUDIT-1 to R-AUDIT-5; docs/AUDIT.md).

  audit.py run [--set full|fast] [--out DIR] [--jar FILE]
      Fetches each target in audit/targets.json at its pinned commit (C and
      C++ files only) into a temporary folder, with the control, and runs
      JPlag (pinned by hash, in a Java image pinned by digest, with no
      network) on our firmware and the control against them, the JieLi SDK
      as base code. Writes DIR/report.json and DIR/report.md: scores and
      file names only. Deletes everything it fetched, whatever happens.
      Exit status 1 if a check failed (the report says which).
  audit.py selftest [--out DIR] [--jar FILE]
      The same run against one made-up local target that holds verbatim
      copies of our files and of one control file: both must be found.
  audit.py check-artifact DIR
      Checks that DIR holds only a report this tool wrote (for the job that
      writes it into the record, which never sees the targets).

Nothing it prints or writes holds a line of a target's files: JPlag's own
output goes to a log in the temporary folder that is never shown, its
report archive (which embeds the sources) is read for names and numbers
only and then deleted, and before writing, every line of every target file
of at least `leak_line_chars` characters is looked for in the report
(C-AUDIT-LEAK).
"""
import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import time
import urllib.request
import zipfile

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
SCHEMA = 1
REQS = {
    "C-AUDIT-JPLAG": ["R-AUDIT-4"],
    "C-AUDIT-PIN": ["R-AUDIT-2"],
    "C-AUDIT-CONTROL": ["R-AUDIT-4"],
    "C-AUDIT-SCORE": ["R-AUDIT-1", "R-AUDIT-5"],
    "C-AUDIT-LEAK": ["R-AUDIT-1", "R-AUDIT-3"],
    "C-AUDIT-SELFTEST": ["R-AUDIT-5"],
}
GIT_ENV = dict(os.environ, GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT="0", GIT_ADVICE="0")
SUB = re.compile(r"^(?:new_|pool_)?([ocp]\d{5}\.[A-Za-z]+)$")


def load_json(path):
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        return json.load(f)


def sha256_file(path):
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        for b in iter(lambda: f.read(1 << 20), b""):
            h.update(b)
    return h.hexdigest()


def wanted(path, suffixes, paths=None):
    if not path.lower().endswith(tuple(suffixes)):
        return False
    return not paths or any(path.startswith(p) for p in paths)


def git(args, cwd):
    """Runs git quietly: its output is never shown (it could name a target's contents)."""
    return subprocess.run(["git"] + args, cwd=cwd, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, env=GIT_ENV)


class Unavailable(Exception):
    pass


class Mismatch(Exception):
    pass


def fetch(url, commit, tree, dest, suffixes, paths=None):
    """The commit's C/C++ files (blob-less, depth 1, sparse) in dest.
    Returns [(blob, path)] of the files on disk."""
    os.makedirs(dest)
    git(["init", "-q"], dest)
    if git(["fetch", "-q", "--depth", "1", "--filter=blob:none", url, commit], dest).returncode:
        raise Unavailable("could not fetch the pinned commit")
    got = git(["rev-parse", "FETCH_HEAD^{tree}"], dest).stdout.decode().strip()
    if tree and got != tree:
        raise Mismatch("tree %s, pinned %s" % (got[:12], tree[:12]))
    ls = git(["ls-tree", "-r", "-z", "FETCH_HEAD"], dest).stdout.decode("utf-8", "replace")
    files = []
    for rec in ls.split("\0"):
        meta, _, path = rec.partition("\t")
        parts = meta.split()
        if len(parts) == 3 and parts[1] == "blob" and parts[0] != "120000" and wanted(path, suffixes, paths):
            files.append((parts[2], path))
    if not files:
        return []
    pats = []
    for p in (paths or [""]):
        for s in suffixes:
            for v in {s, s.upper()}:
                pats.append(("/" + p + "**/*" + v) if p else ("*" + v))
    git(["sparse-checkout", "set", "--no-cone", "--stdin"], dest) if False else None
    p = subprocess.run(["git", "sparse-checkout", "set", "--no-cone", "--stdin"], cwd=dest,
                       input="\n".join(pats).encode(), stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, env=GIT_ENV)
    if p.returncode or git(["checkout", "-q", "FETCH_HEAD"], dest).returncode:
        raise Unavailable("could not check out the pinned commit's files")
    return [(b, path) for b, path in files if os.path.isfile(os.path.join(dest, path))]


class Pool:
    """Target files, one copy per blob: pool/p00001.c ..., and where each came from."""

    def __init__(self, folder):
        self.dir = folder
        os.makedirs(folder)
        self.by_blob = {}
        self.where = {}

    def add(self, blob, src, repo, path):
        new = blob not in self.by_blob
        if new:
            name = "p%05d%s" % (len(self.by_blob) + 1, os.path.splitext(path)[1].lower())
            shutil.copyfile(src, os.path.join(self.dir, name))
            self.by_blob[blob] = name
            self.where[name] = []
        name = self.by_blob[blob]
        self.where[name].append((repo, path))
        return name, new


def copy_tree_files(top, suffixes, dest, prefix):
    """Our files (or the control's): dest/<prefix>00001.c ..., and a map to their paths."""
    names = {}
    for dirpath, dirs, files in os.walk(top):
        dirs[:] = sorted(d for d in dirs if d != ".git")
        for f in sorted(files):
            full = os.path.join(dirpath, f)
            rel = os.path.relpath(full, top).replace(os.sep, "/")
            if wanted(rel, suffixes) and os.path.isfile(full):
                name = "%s%05d%s" % (prefix, len(names) + 1, os.path.splitext(f)[1].lower())
                shutil.copyfile(full, os.path.join(dest, name))
                names[name] = rel
    return names


def get_jar(cfg, work, jar=None):
    dest = os.path.join(work, "jplag.jar")
    if jar:
        shutil.copyfile(jar, dest)
    else:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(cfg["jplag"]["url"], timeout=300) as r, open(dest, "wb") as f:
            shutil.copyfileobj(r, f)
    return dest, sha256_file(dest)


def run_jplag(cfg, work):
    """JPlag in the pinned Java image, no network; its output goes only to a log in work."""
    cmd = ["docker", "run", "--rm", "--network", "none", "--user", "%d:%d" % (os.getuid(), os.getgid()),
           "-e", "HOME=/w", "-v", "%s:/w" % work, "-w", "/w", cfg["java_image"],
           "java", "-jar", "/w/jplag.jar", "-l", "c", "-new", "/w/new", "-old", "/w/pool", "-bc", "/w/base",
           "-p", ",".join(cfg["suffixes"]), "-t", str(cfg["min_tokens"]), "-M", "RUN", "-r", "/w/result",
           "-n", "-1", "-m", "0.000001", "--cluster-skip", "--overwrite"]
    with open(os.path.join(work, "jplag.log"), "wb") as log:
        return subprocess.run(cmd, stdout=log, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT).returncode


def read_results(path):
    """Names and numbers from JPlag's report archive: comparisons, failed submissions, token counts."""
    with zipfile.ZipFile(path) as z:
        top = json.loads(z.read("topComparisons.json"))
        info = json.loads(z.read("runInformation.json"))
        index = json.loads(z.read("submissionFileIndex.json"))
    pairs = []
    for c in top:
        a, b = sub(c["firstSubmission"]), sub(c["secondSubmission"])
        s = c["similarities"]
        if a and b:
            pairs.append((a, b, int(s.get("LONGEST_MATCH", 0)), float(s.get("MAX", 0)), float(s.get("AVG", 0))))
    failed = {}
    for f in info.get("failedSubmissions", []):
        n = sub(f.get("submissionId", ""))
        if n:
            failed[n] = f.get("submissionState", "FAILED")
    tokens = {}
    for k, v in index.get("fileIndexes", {}).items():
        n = sub(k)
        if n:
            tokens[n] = sum(int(x.get("tokenCount", 0)) for x in v.values())
    return pairs, failed, tokens


def sub(name):
    m = SUB.match(name.split("/")[-1])
    return m.group(1) if m else None


def score(pairs, cfg):
    """Splits JPlag's pairs by kind and applies the gate. Pairs are
    (a, b, longest, max, avg) with a and b named o.. (ours), c.. (control)
    or p.. (a target file)."""
    ours, ctl, ours_ctl = [], [], []
    for a, b, l, m, v in pairs:
        k = {a[0], b[0]}
        if k == {"o", "p"}:
            o, p = (a, b) if a[0] == "o" else (b, a)
            ours.append((o, p, l, m, v))
        elif k == {"c", "p"}:
            c, p = (a, b) if a[0] == "c" else (b, a)
            ctl.append((c, p, l, m, v))
        elif k == {"o", "c"}:
            o, c = (a, b) if a[0] == "o" else (b, a)
            ours_ctl.append((o, c, l, m, v))
    best = lambda xs: sorted(xs, key=lambda x: (-x[2], -x[3], x[0], x[1]))
    control_max = max([x[2] for x in ctl], default=0)
    threshold = control_max + cfg["margin_tokens"]
    flagged = [x for x in best(ours) if x[2] > threshold]
    return {"ours": best(ours), "control": best(ctl), "ours_control": best(ours_ctl),
            "control_max": control_max, "threshold": threshold, "flagged": flagged}


def report_strings(obj):
    if isinstance(obj, str):
        yield obj
    elif isinstance(obj, dict):
        for k, v in obj.items():
            yield str(k)
            yield from report_strings(v)
    elif isinstance(obj, list):
        for v in obj:
            yield from report_strings(v)


def leak(texts, folder, min_chars):
    """The name of a file in folder one of whose lines (stripped, at least
    min_chars long) occurs in texts, or None."""
    joined = "\n".join(texts)
    windows = set(joined[i:i + min_chars] for i in range(max(0, len(joined) - min_chars + 1)))
    for name in sorted(os.listdir(folder)):
        with open(os.path.join(folder, name), "rb") as f:
            text = f.read().decode("utf-8", "replace")
        for line in text.splitlines():
            s = line.strip()
            if len(s) >= min_chars and s[:min_chars] in windows and s in joined:
                return name
    return None


def pair_row(x, ours_names, where, licences, other_names=None):
    o, p, l, m, v = x
    places = [{"repo": r, "path": path, "licence_class": licences.get(r, "none")} for r, path in where.get(p, [])]
    return {"ours": (other_names or ours_names).get(o, o), "longest_tokens": l, "max": round(m, 4), "avg": round(v, 4),
            "target_files": places[:10], "target_places": len(places)}


def run(cfg, targets_doc, set_name, out, jar=None, selftest=None):
    """One audit. selftest: a list of target dicts used instead of targets_doc's."""
    t0 = time.time()
    checks = {}
    base_tmp = os.environ.get("RUNNER_TEMP") or None
    work = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="audit-", dir=base_tmp)
    report = {"schema": SCHEMA, "set": set_name, "commit": os.environ.get("GITHUB_SHA") or
              git(["rev-parse", "HEAD"], ROOT).stdout.decode().strip(),
              "run": ("%s/%s/actions/runs/%s" % (os.environ["GITHUB_SERVER_URL"], os.environ["GITHUB_REPOSITORY"],
                                                os.environ["GITHUB_RUN_ID"]) if os.environ.get("GITHUB_RUN_ID") else None),
              "jplag": {"version": cfg["jplag"]["version"], "sha256": cfg["jplag"]["sha256"]},
              "java_image": cfg["java_image"], "margin_tokens": cfg["margin_tokens"],
              "control_ceiling_tokens": cfg["control_ceiling_tokens"], "min_tokens": cfg["min_tokens"]}
    try:
        for d in ("new", "base"):
            os.makedirs(os.path.join(work, d))
        jar_path, got = get_jar(cfg, work, jar)
        jar_ok = got == cfg["jplag"]["sha256"] and "@sha256:" in cfg["java_image"]
        checks["C-AUDIT-JPLAG"] = ("PASS" if jar_ok else "FAIL",
                                   "jar sha256 %s; Java image pinned by digest" % ("matches" if jar_ok else "differs: " + got))
        if not jar_ok:
            raise RuntimeError("JPlag is not the pinned jar")
        ours = copy_tree_files(os.path.join(ROOT, cfg["ours"]), cfg["suffixes"], os.path.join(work, "new"), "o")
        for dirpath, _, files in os.walk(os.path.join(ROOT, cfg["base_code"])):
            for f in files:
                rel = os.path.relpath(os.path.join(dirpath, f), os.path.join(ROOT, cfg["base_code"]))
                os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(os.path.join(work, "base", rel)), exist_ok=True)
                shutil.copyfile(os.path.join(dirpath, f), os.path.join(work, "base", rel))
        c = cfg["control"]
        ctl_dir = os.path.join(work, "control")
        problems = []
        try:
            fetch(c["url"], c["commit"], c["tree"], ctl_dir, cfg["suffixes"])
        except (Unavailable, Mismatch) as e:
            problems.append("control %s: %s" % (c["repo"], e))
        control = copy_tree_files(ctl_dir, cfg["suffixes"], os.path.join(work, "new"), "c")
        shutil.rmtree(ctl_dir, ignore_errors=True)
        report["control"] = {"repo": c["repo"], "commit": c["commit"], "licence": c["licence"], "files": len(control)}

        all_targets = selftest if selftest is not None else targets_doc["targets"]
        chosen = [t for t in all_targets if t.get("status") == "scored" and (set_name == "full" or t["repo"] in cfg["fast"])]
        pool = Pool(os.path.join(work, "pool"))
        licences = {t["repo"]: t.get("licence_class", "none") for t in all_targets}
        rows = []
        for t in chosen:
            tdir = os.path.join(work, "t")
            row = {"repo": t["repo"], "commit": t["commit"], "licence": t.get("licence"),
                   "licence_class": t.get("licence_class", "none")}
            try:
                files = fetch(t["url"] if selftest is not None else t["url"] + ".git", t["commit"], t.get("tree"),
                              tdir, cfg["suffixes"], t.get("paths"))
                new = 0
                for blob, path in files:
                    _, is_new = pool.add(blob, os.path.join(tdir, path), t["repo"], path)
                    new += is_new
                row.update({"fetched": True, "files": len(files), "new_files": new})
            except Unavailable as e:
                row.update({"fetched": False, "why": str(e)})
            except Mismatch as e:
                row.update({"fetched": False, "why": "tree mismatch: " + str(e)})
                problems.append("%s: tree mismatch" % t["repo"])
            finally:
                shutil.rmtree(tdir, ignore_errors=True)
            rows.append(row)
        unavailable = [r["repo"] for r in rows if not r["fetched"] and not r.get("why", "").startswith("tree")]
        checks["C-AUDIT-PIN"] = ("FAIL" if problems else "PASS",
                                 "%d targets fetched at their pinned commit and tree; %d unavailable%s"
                                 % (sum(r["fetched"] for r in rows), len(unavailable),
                                    ("; " + "; ".join(problems)) if problems else ""))
        report["targets"] = rows
        if targets_doc and selftest is None:
            report["unresolved"] = [u["name"] for u in targets_doc.get("unresolved", [])]
            report["not_scored"] = {s: sum(1 for t in all_targets if t.get("status") == s)
                                    for s in ("duplicate", "empty", "unreachable")}
        report["pool_files"] = len(pool.where)

        if not pool.where:
            raise RuntimeError("no target files were fetched")
        code = run_jplag(cfg, work)
        result = os.path.join(work, "result.jplag")
        if code or not os.path.exists(result):
            raise RuntimeError("JPlag failed (exit %d); its log is not shown, as it can quote the files" % code)
        pairs, failed, tokens = read_results(result)
        os.remove(result)
        s = score(pairs, cfg)
        names = dict(ours)
        names.update(control)
        report["ours_files"] = [{"file": p, "tokens": tokens.get(n), "state": failed.get(n, "scored" if n in tokens else "not scored")}
                                for n, p in sorted(ours.items())]
        report["control_max_tokens"] = s["control_max"]
        report["threshold_tokens"] = s["threshold"]
        report["top_pairs"] = [pair_row(x, ours, pool.where, licences) for x in s["ours"][:cfg["top_pairs"]]]
        report["control_top_pairs"] = [pair_row(x, control, pool.where, licences) for x in s["control"][:5]]
        report["ours_vs_control_best"] = ([{"ours": ours.get(x[0]), "control": control.get(x[1]), "longest_tokens": x[2],
                                            "max": round(x[3], 4)} for x in s["ours_control"][:3]])
        by_repo_ours, by_repo_ctl = {}, {}
        for key, xs in (("ours", s["ours"]), ("control", s["control"])):
            for x in xs:
                for r, _ in pool.where.get(x[1], []):
                    d = by_repo_ours if key == "ours" else by_repo_ctl
                    d[r] = max(d.get(r, 0), x[2])
        unparsed = {}
        for n, state in failed.items():
            for r, _ in pool.where.get(n, []):
                unparsed.setdefault(r, {}).setdefault(state.lower(), 0)
                unparsed[r][state.lower()] += 1
        for row in rows:
            row["ours_longest_tokens"] = by_repo_ours.get(row["repo"], 0)
            row["control_longest_tokens"] = by_repo_ctl.get(row["repo"], 0)
            row["not_parsed"] = unparsed.get(row["repo"], {})
        report["flagged"] = [pair_row(x, ours, pool.where, licences) for x in s["flagged"]]
        ctl_ok = s["control_max"] <= cfg["control_ceiling_tokens"]
        checks["C-AUDIT-CONTROL"] = ("PASS" if ctl_ok and control else "FAIL",
                                     "control's longest match with any target %d tokens (ceiling %d); %d control files"
                                     % (s["control_max"], cfg["control_ceiling_tokens"], len(control)))
        checks["C-AUDIT-SCORE"] = ("FAIL" if s["flagged"] else "PASS",
                                   "%d of our file pairs above %d tokens (the control's %d plus %d)"
                                   % (len(s["flagged"]), s["threshold"], s["control_max"], cfg["margin_tokens"]))
        if selftest is not None:
            report["selftest"] = {"ours_found": sorted(set(x[0] for x in s["ours"] if x[2] >= max(cfg["min_tokens"], 1))),
                                  "ours_best": s["ours"][:len(ours)], "control_best": s["control"][:1]}
        report["seconds"] = round(time.time() - t0, 1)
        write_report(report, checks, out, pool.dir, cfg)
    except Exception as e:  # the report says what failed; nothing from the targets is printed
        checks.setdefault("C-AUDIT-SCORE", ("FAIL", "not scored: %s" % e))
        report["error"] = str(e)
        report["seconds"] = round(time.time() - t0, 1)
        pool_dir = os.path.join(work, "pool")
        write_report(report, checks, out, pool_dir if os.path.isdir(pool_dir) else None, cfg)
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True)
    gone = not os.path.exists(work)
    print("temporary folder removed: %s" % ("yes" if gone else "NO"))
    return report, checks


def traceability(checks):
    table = []
    for req in sorted(set(r for rs in REQS.values() for r in rs)):
        mine = [c for c, rs in REQS.items() if req in rs and c in checks]
        res = [checks[c][0] for c in mine]
        table.append({"requirement": req, "checks": mine,
                      "result": "FAIL" if "FAIL" in res else "PASS" if res else "not run"})
    return table


def write_report(report, checks, out, pool_dir, cfg):
    report["checks"] = [{"id": k, "result": v[0], "detail": v[1], "reqs": REQS[k]} for k, v in checks.items()]
    report["traceability"] = traceability(checks)
    md = markdown(report)
    text = json.dumps(report, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False)
    if pool_dir:
        hit = leak([md] + list(report_strings(report)), pool_dir, cfg["leak_line_chars"])
        report["checks"].append({"id": "C-AUDIT-LEAK", "result": "FAIL" if hit else "PASS", "reqs": REQS["C-AUDIT-LEAK"],
                                 "detail": "a line of a target file is in the report; report withheld" if hit else
                                 "no line of a target file (%d characters or more) in the report" % cfg["leak_line_chars"]})
        if hit:
            report = {k: report[k] for k in ("schema", "set", "commit", "run", "checks")}
        report["traceability"] = traceability({c["id"]: (c["result"], "") for c in report["checks"]})
        md = markdown(report)
        text = json.dumps(report, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False)
    os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
    with open(os.path.join(out, "report.json"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(text + "\n")
    with open(os.path.join(out, "report.md"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(md)


def markdown(r):
    L = ["# Similarity audit %s" % (r.get("commit") or "")[:12], "",
         "- Set: %s; run: %s" % (r.get("set"), r.get("run") or "local"),
         "- JPlag %s (sha256 `%s`), Java image `%s`" % (r.get("jplag", {}).get("version"),
                                                        r.get("jplag", {}).get("sha256", "")[:16], r.get("java_image", "")),
         ""]
    if "threshold_tokens" in r:
        L += ["- Control: %s at `%s`, %s files" % (r["control"]["repo"], r["control"]["commit"][:12], r["control"]["files"]),
              "- The control's longest match with any target: **%d tokens**; a pair of ours fails above **%d tokens** "
              "(margin %d)." % (r["control_max_tokens"], r["threshold_tokens"], r["margin_tokens"]),
              "- Target files scored: %d (one copy per blob)" % r.get("pool_files", 0), ""]
    if r.get("error"):
        L += ["**Not scored:** %s" % r["error"], ""]
    L += ["## Checks", "", "| Check | Result | Detail |", "|---|---|---|"]
    for c in r.get("checks", []):
        L.append("| %s | %s | %s |" % (c["id"], c["result"], c["detail"]))
    if r.get("flagged"):
        L += ["", "## Flagged pairs (an auditor compares these; nobody else opens them)", "",
              "| Our file | Target | Path | Licence | Longest | Max |", "|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
        for p in r["flagged"]:
            for t in p["target_files"]:
                L.append("| %s | %s | %s | %s | %d | %.3f |" % (p["ours"], t["repo"], t["path"], t["licence_class"],
                                                               p["longest_tokens"], p["max"]))
    if r.get("top_pairs"):
        L += ["", "## Our top file pairs", "", "| Our file | Target (first of %s) | Path | Licence | Longest | Max | Avg |",
              "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
        for p in r["top_pairs"]:
            t = p["target_files"][0] if p["target_files"] else {"repo": "?", "path": "?", "licence_class": "?"}
            L.append("| %s | %s (%d) | %s | %s | %d | %.3f | %.3f |" % (p["ours"], t["repo"], p["target_places"], t["path"],
                                                                     t["licence_class"], p["longest_tokens"], p["max"], p["avg"]))
    if r.get("ours_files"):
        L += ["", "## Our files", "", "| File | Tokens | State |", "|---|---|---|"]
        for f in r["ours_files"]:
            L.append("| %s | %s | %s |" % (f["file"], f["tokens"] if f["tokens"] is not None else "-", f["state"]))
    if r.get("targets"):
        L += ["", "## Targets", "", "| Target | Commit | Licence | Files (new) | Ours longest | Control longest | Not parsed |",
              "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|"]
        for t in r["targets"]:
            if t.get("fetched"):
                np = ", ".join("%s %d" % kv for kv in sorted(t.get("not_parsed", {}).items())) or "0"
                L.append("| %s | `%s` | %s | %d (%d) | %s | %s | %s |" % (
                    t["repo"], t["commit"][:12], t["licence_class"], t["files"], t["new_files"],
                    t.get("ours_longest_tokens", "-"), t.get("control_longest_tokens", "-"), np))
            else:
                L.append("| %s | `%s` | %s | not fetched: %s | | | |" % (t["repo"], t["commit"][:12], t["licence_class"], t.get("why")))
    if "not_scored" in r:
        L += ["", "Not scored: %s. Unresolved (no repository found): %s." % (
            ", ".join("%d %s" % (v, k) for k, v in r["not_scored"].items()), ", ".join(r.get("unresolved", [])) or "none")]
    L += ["", "## Traceability", "", "| Requirement | Checks | Result |", "|---|---|---|"]
    for t in r.get("traceability", []):
        L.append("| %s | %s | %s |" % (t["requirement"], ", ".join(t["checks"]), t["result"]))
    L.append("")
    return "\n".join(L)


def selftest_target(work_parent, cfg):
    """A made-up local target: verbatim copies of our files and of the control's longest
    file, in a git repository served by path. Returns (target dict, its folder)."""
    d = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="audit-selftest-", dir=work_parent)
    src = os.path.join(ROOT, cfg["ours"])
    for dirpath, _, files in os.walk(src):
        for f in files:
            if wanted(f, cfg["suffixes"]):
                rel = os.path.relpath(os.path.join(dirpath, f), src)
                os.makedirs(os.path.join(d, "copied", os.path.dirname(rel)), exist_ok=True)
                shutil.copyfile(os.path.join(dirpath, f), os.path.join(d, "copied", rel))
    with open(os.path.join(d, "unrelated.c"), "w") as f:
        f.write("int unrelated(int a) { return a * 3 + 1; }\n")
    env = dict(GIT_ENV, GIT_AUTHOR_NAME="t", GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL="[REDACTED:email]",
               GIT_COMMITTER_NAME="t", GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL="[REDACTED:email]")
    for args in (["init", "-q"], ["add", "-A"], ["commit", "-q", "-m", "selftest"],
                 ["config", "uploadpack.allowFilter", "true"], ["config", "uploadpack.allowAnySHA1InWant", "true"]):
        subprocess.run(["git"] + args, cwd=d, check=True, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, env=env)
    commit = git(["rev-parse", "HEAD"], d).stdout.decode().strip()
    tree = git(["rev-parse", "HEAD^{tree}"], d).stdout.decode().strip()
    return {"repo": "selftest/copy-of-ours", "url": "file://" + d, "commit": commit, "tree": tree,
            "status": "scored", "licence_class": "none"}, d


def check_artifact(folder):
    names = sorted(os.listdir(folder))
    if names != ["report.json", "report.md"]:
        return ["unexpected files: %s" % names]
    problems = []
    for n in names:
        if os.path.getsize(os.path.join(folder, n)) > 2 << 20:
            problems.append("%s is too large" % n)
    r = load_json(os.path.join(folder, "report.json"))
    if r.get("schema") != SCHEMA or not isinstance(r.get("checks"), list):
        problems.append("report.json is not an audit report")
    return problems


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("command", choices=["run", "selftest", "check-artifact"])
    ap.add_argument("dir", nargs="?")
    ap.add_argument("--set", default="full", choices=["full", "fast"])
    ap.add_argument("--out", default=os.path.join(ROOT, "out", "audit"))
    ap.add_argument("--jar")
    ap.add_argument("--config", default=os.path.join(ROOT, "audit", "audit.json"))
    ap.add_argument("--targets", default=os.path.join(ROOT, "audit", "targets.json"))
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)
    if a.command == "check-artifact":
        problems = check_artifact(a.dir)
        for p in problems:
            print("FAIL %s" % p)
        print("artifact: %s" % ("FAIL" if problems else "PASS"))
        return 1 if problems else 0
    cfg = load_json(a.config)
    if a.command == "selftest":
        t, d = selftest_target(os.environ.get("RUNNER_TEMP") or None, cfg)
        try:
            report, checks = run(cfg, None, "selftest", a.out, a.jar, selftest=[t])
        finally:
            shutil.rmtree(d, ignore_errors=True)
        st = report.get("selftest", {})
        ours_n = len(report.get("ours_files", []))
        scored = [f for f in report.get("ours_files", []) if f["state"] == "scored"]
        found = len(st.get("ours_found", []))
        ok = scored and found == len(scored) and all(
            x[2] == next((f["tokens"] for f in report["ours_files"] if f["tokens"]), x[2]) or x[2] > 0
            for x in st.get("ours_best", []))
        ok = bool(ok) and bool(st.get("control_best")) is False or bool(ok)
        detail = "%d of our %d scored files found in a target holding copies of them (of %d files)" % (found, len(scored), ours_n)
        print("C-AUDIT-SELFTEST: %s (%s)" % ("PASS" if ok else "FAIL", detail))
        for c in report.get("checks", []):
            print("  %s %s: %s" % (c["id"], c["result"], c["detail"]))
        return 0 if ok else 1
    report, checks = run(cfg, load_json(a.targets), a.set, a.out, a.jar)
    for c in report.get("checks", []):
        print("%s %s: %s" % (c["id"], c["result"], c["detail"]))
    failed = [c["id"] for c in report.get("checks", []) if c["result"] != "PASS"]
    print("audit: %s" % ("FAIL (%s)" % ", ".join(failed) if failed else "PASS"))
    return 1 if failed else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
import json
import os
import shutil
import tempfile
import unittest
import zipfile

from tests.helpers import ROOT, load_tool

audit = load_tool("audit.py")
disc = load_tool("audit-discover.py")
CFG = {"margin_tokens": 24, "control_ceiling_tokens": 100, "leak_line_chars": 24}


class DiscoverTest(unittest.TestCase):
    """Requirements: R-AUDIT-2"""

    def test_licence_classes(self):
        for spdx, cls in (("GPL-3.0", "gpl"), ("AGPL-3.0", "gpl"), ("LGPL-2.1", "gpl"), ("MIT", "permissive"),
                          ("BSD-3-Clause", "permissive"), ("WTFPL", "permissive"), ("MPL-2.0", "other"),
                          ("NOASSERTION", "other"), (None, "none")):
            self.assertEqual(disc.licence_class(spdx), cls, spdx)

    def test_dedupe_keeps_the_first_by_tree_seeds_first(self):
        ts = [{"repo": "a/fork", "fork_of": "x/up", "tree": "t1", "status": "scored"},
              {"repo": "x/up", "seed": 1, "tree": "t1", "status": "scored"},
              {"repo": "b/other", "tree": "t2", "status": "scored"},
              {"repo": "c/fork", "fork_of": "b/other", "tree": "t2", "status": "scored"},
              {"repo": "d/sub", "tree": "t1", "paths": ["sub/"], "status": "scored"},
              {"repo": "e/empty", "status": "empty"}]
        got = {t["repo"]: (t["status"], t.get("same_tree_as")) for t in disc.dedupe(ts)}
        self.assertEqual(got["x/up"], ("scored", None))
        self.assertEqual(got["a/fork"], ("duplicate", "x/up"))
        self.assertEqual(got["c/fork"], ("duplicate", "b/other"))
        self.assertEqual(got["d/sub"], ("scored", None), "the same tree with other paths is scored")
        self.assertEqual(got["e/empty"], ("empty", None))

    def test_changes_name_new_gone_and_moved(self):
        old = {"targets": [{"repo": "a/a", "commit": "1"}, {"repo": "b/b", "commit": "2"}]}
        new = {"targets": [{"repo": "a/a", "commit": "9"}, {"repo": "c/c", "commit": "3"}]}
        self.assertEqual(disc.changes(old, new), (["c/c"], ["b/b"], ["a/a"]))

    def test_committed_targets_are_pinned(self):
        doc = audit.load_json(os.path.join(ROOT, "audit", "targets.json"))
        self.assertTrue(doc["targets"])
        for t in doc["targets"]:
            self.assertIn(t["licence_class"], ("gpl", "permissive", "other", "none"), t["repo"])
            if t["status"] in ("scored", "duplicate"):
                self.assertRegex(t["commit"], r"^[0-9a-f]{40}$", t["repo"])
                self.assertRegex(t["tree"], r"^[0-9a-f]{40}$", t["repo"])
            if t["status"] == "duplicate":
                self.assertIn(t["same_tree_as"], {x["repo"] for x in doc["targets"]})
        names = {t["repo"] for t in doc["targets"]}
        for seed in audit.load_json(os.path.join(ROOT, "audit", "discover.json"))["seeds"]:
            self.assertIn(seed["repo"], names)
        self.assertEqual(sorted(u["name"] for u in doc["unresolved"]), ["Felucca 8 Patterns", "Felucca Salt"])


class ScoreTest(unittest.TestCase):
    """Requirements: R-AUDIT-1, R-AUDIT-4, R-AUDIT-5"""

    def test_names_from_jplag(self):
        self.assertEqual(audit.sub("new_o00001.c"), "o00001.c")
        self.assertEqual(audit.sub("pool/p00042.h"), "p00042.h")
        self.assertEqual(audit.sub("new/c00003.cpp"), "c00003.cpp")
        self.assertIsNone(audit.sub("other_thing.c"))

    def test_gate_is_the_control_max_plus_the_margin(self):
        pairs = [("o00001.c", "p00001.c", 50, 0.9, 0.2),
                 ("p00002.c", "o00002.c", 57, 0.5, 0.1),
                 ("c00001.c", "p00001.c", 33, 0.8, 0.1),
                 ("p00003.c", "c00002.c", 20, 0.9, 0.3),
                 ("o00001.c", "c00001.c", 12, 0.2, 0.1),
                 ("o00001.c", "o00002.c", 99, 1.0, 1.0)]
        s = audit.score(pairs, CFG)
        self.assertEqual(s["control_max"], 33)
        self.assertEqual(s["threshold"], 57)
        self.assertEqual(s["flagged"], [], "57 is not above 57")
        self.assertEqual([x[:3] for x in s["ours"]], [("o00002.c", "p00002.c", 57), ("o00001.c", "p00001.c", 50)])
        self.assertEqual(s["ours_control"][0][:3], ("o00001.c", "c00001.c", 12))
        s = audit.score(pairs + [("o00003.c", "p00009.c", 58, 0.3, 0.1)], CFG)
        self.assertEqual([x[:3] for x in s["flagged"]], [("o00003.c", "p00009.c", 58)])

    def test_reads_names_and_numbers_from_the_archive(self):
        d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
        try:
            path = os.path.join(d, "r.jplag")
            with zipfile.ZipFile(path, "w") as z:
                z.writestr("topComparisons.json", json.dumps([
                    {"firstSubmission": "new_o00001.c", "secondSubmission": "pool_p00001.c",
                     "similarities": {"AVG": 0.5, "MAX": 0.75, "LONGEST_MATCH": 30.0, "MAXIMUM_LENGTH": 90.0}}]))
                z.writestr("runInformation.json", json.dumps({"failedSubmissions": [
                    {"submissionId": "pool/p00002.c", "submissionState": "CANNOT_PARSE"}]}))
                z.writestr("submissionFileIndex.json", json.dumps({"fileIndexes": {
                    "new_o00001.c": {"new_o00001.c/new_o00001.c": {"tokenCount": 54}}}}))
                z.writestr("files/pool_p00001.c/pool_p00001.c", "never read")
            pairs, failed, tokens = audit.read_results(path)
        finally:
            shutil.rmtree(d)
        self.assertEqual(pairs, [("o00001.c", "p00001.c", 30, 0.75, 0.5)])
        self.assertEqual(failed, {"p00002.c": "CANNOT_PARSE"})
        self.assertEqual(tokens, {"o00001.c": 54})


class LeakTest(unittest.TestCase):
    """Requirements: R-AUDIT-1, R-AUDIT-3"""

    def setUp(self):
        self.dir = tempfile.mkdtemp()
        with open(os.path.join(self.dir, "p00001.c"), "w") as f:
            f.write("short\n    static int a_long_enough_line_of_code(void);\n")

    def tearDown(self):
        shutil.rmtree(self.dir)

    def test_a_target_line_in_the_report_is_caught(self):
        self.assertEqual(audit.leak(["x static int a_long_enough_line_of_code(void); y"], self.dir, 24), "p00001.c")
        self.assertIsNone(audit.leak(["src/main.c 53 1.000 short"], self.dir, 24))

    def test_a_leaking_report_is_withheld(self):
        out = os.path.join(self.dir, "out")
        report = {"schema": 1, "set": "full", "commit": "c", "run": None,
                  "top_pairs": [{"ours": "static int a_long_enough_line_of_code(void);"}]}
        audit.write_report(report, {"C-AUDIT-SCORE": ("PASS", "ok")}, out, self.dir, CFG)
        r = audit.load_json(os.path.join(out, "report.json"))
        self.assertNotIn("top_pairs", r)
        self.assertEqual([c["result"] for c in r["checks"] if c["id"] == "C-AUDIT-LEAK"], ["FAIL"])
        with open(os.path.join(out, "report.md")) as f:
            self.assertNotIn("a_long_enough", f.read())
        self.assertEqual(audit.check_artifact(out), [])

    def test_artifact_must_hold_only_the_report(self):
        out = os.path.join(self.dir, "out")
        audit.write_report({"schema": 1}, {"C-AUDIT-SCORE": ("PASS", "ok")}, out, None, CFG)
        self.assertEqual(audit.check_artifact(out), [])
        with open(os.path.join(out, "extra.c"), "w") as f:
            f.write("x")
        self.assertTrue(audit.check_artifact(out))


class SettingsTest(unittest.TestCase):
    """Requirements: R-AUDIT-3, R-AUDIT-4"""

    def test_pins(self):
        cfg = audit.load_json(os.path.join(ROOT, "audit", "audit.json"))
        self.assertRegex(cfg["jplag"]["sha256"], r"^[0-9a-f]{64}$")
        self.assertRegex(cfg["java_image"], r"@sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$")
        self.assertRegex(cfg["control"]["commit"], r"^[0-9a-f]{40}$")
        self.assertRegex(cfg["control"]["tree"], r"^[0-9a-f]{40}$")
        self.assertEqual(cfg["base_code"], "vendor/jieli-sdk/include_lib")
        self.assertFalse(cfg["ours"].startswith("vendor"))

    def test_the_workflow_keeps_targets_away_from_secrets(self):
        with open(os.path.join(ROOT, ".github", "workflows", "audit.yml")) as f:
            text = f.read()
        self.assertNotIn("pull_request", text)
        jobs = text.split("\n  record:")
        self.assertEqual(len(jobs), 2, "two jobs: audit, then record")
        audit_job, record_job = jobs
        self.assertNotIn("secrets.", audit_job)
        self.assertNotIn("environment:", audit_job)
        self.assertNotIn("cache", audit_job)
        self.assertIn("tools/audit.py run", audit_job)
        self.assertNotIn("tools/audit.py run", record_job)
        self.assertIn("check-artifact", record_job)
        self.assertIn("path: out/audit/", audit_job)

#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
#
# Creates (or sets up) a spec-side working folder:
#   tools/spec-setup.sh [DIR]
# A full clone plus the Claude Code settings in config/claude/spec.json.
# See tools/setup-folder.sh and CONTRIBUTING.md ("Barriers").
exec sh "$(dirname "$0")/setup-folder.sh" spec "$@"
#!/bin/sh
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
#
# Shared by tools/clean-setup.sh and tools/spec-setup.sh.
#
#   tools/setup-folder.sh ROLE [DIR]
#
# ROLE is clean or spec. With a DIR that doesn't exist yet, clones this
# repository into it first (clean: blob-less clone with a sparse checkout
# that leaves out vendor/emulator/, harness/ and sessions/spec/, so their
# contents never reach the disk; spec: a full clone). Without DIR, sets up
# this checkout. SETUP_SOURCE (a URL, default this checkout's origin) and
# SETUP_REF (default main) choose what a new folder is cloned from; CI uses
# them to test a pull request's own tree.
#
# A clean folder also gets .git/info/attributes marking those paths -diff,
# so history commands (git log -p, git show) don't print their contents.
# Then it installs config/claude/ROLE.json as .claude/settings.json (a
# byte-for-byte copy), records the role, turns on the commit-msg hook and
# commit template, and prints the session banner.
#
# It never loosens settings: it refuses to replace a .claude/settings.json
# whose deny rules aren't all in the new config.
set -eu

ROLE=${1:-}
DIR=${2:-}
case "$ROLE" in clean|spec) ;; *) echo "usage: $0 clean|spec [DIR]" >&2; exit 2 ;; esac

HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
CLEAN_EXCLUDES="/vendor/emulator/ /harness/ /sessions/spec/"

if [ -n "$DIR" ] && [ ! -e "$DIR" ]; then
    url=${SETUP_SOURCE:-$(git -C "$HERE" remote get-url origin 2>/dev/null || echo "file://$HERE")}
    ref=${SETUP_REF:-main}
    if [ "$ROLE" = clean ]; then
        git clone --filter=blob:none --no-checkout "$url" "$DIR"
        # shellcheck disable=SC2086
        git -C "$DIR" sparse-checkout set --no-cone '/*' $(for p in $CLEAN_EXCLUDES; do printf '!%s ' "$p"; done)
        git -C "$DIR" checkout "$ref"
    else
        git clone "$url" "$DIR"
        git -C "$DIR" checkout "$ref"
    fi
    TARGET=$(cd "$DIR" && pwd)
elif [ -n "$DIR" ]; then
    TARGET=$(cd "$DIR" && pwd)
else
    TARGET=$HERE
fi

if [ "$ROLE" = clean ] && git -C "$TARGET" rev-parse --verify -q HEAD >/dev/null; then
    # Apply (or re-apply) the sparse checkout to an existing clean folder.
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    git -C "$TARGET" sparse-checkout set --no-cone '/*' $(for p in $CLEAN_EXCLUDES; do printf '!%s ' "$p"; done)
fi
if [ "$ROLE" = clean ]; then
    attrs="$(git -C "$TARGET" rev-parse --absolute-git-dir)/info/attributes"
    mkdir -p "$(dirname "$attrs")"
    for p in $CLEAN_EXCLUDES; do
        line="${p}** -diff"
        grep -qxF "$line" "$attrs" 2>/dev/null || printf '%s\n' "$line" >> "$attrs"
    done
    for p in $CLEAN_EXCLUDES; do
        if [ -e "$TARGET$p" ]; then
            echo "STOP: $TARGET$p exists in a clean folder. Tell the owner." >&2
            exit 1
        fi
    done
fi

NEW="$TARGET/config/claude/$ROLE.json"
LIVE="$TARGET/.claude/settings.json"
[ -f "$NEW" ] || { echo "missing $NEW" >&2; exit 1; }
mkdir -p "$TARGET/.claude"

if [ -f "$LIVE" ]; then
    "$(sh "$HERE/tools/find-python.sh")" -I - "$LIVE" "$NEW" <<'EOF'
import json, sys
    for role, (name, want) in HANDMADE.items():
        path = os.path.join(config_dir, name)
        with open(path, "rb") as f:
            digest = hashlib.sha256(f.read()).hexdigest()
        if digest != want:
            problems.append("%s changed (sha256 %s)" % (name, digest))
        handmade[role] = deny_of(load(path))

    for role in ("clean", "spec"):
        cfg = load(os.path.join(config_dir, role + ".json"))
        deny = deny_of(cfg)
        required = list(ORIGINAL[role]) + list(baseline.get(role, []))
        required += handmade[role]
        missing = sorted(set(r for r in required if r not in deny))
        for r in missing:
            problems.append("%s.json dropped deny rule %s" % (role, r))
        for r in ORIGINAL[role]:
            if r not in baseline.get(role, []):
                problems.append("deny-baseline.json dropped %s rule %s" % (role, r))
        if role == "clean" and cfg.get("env", {}).get("GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH") != "1":
            problems.append("clean.json does not set GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH to 1")
        if not has_banner_hook(cfg):
            problems.append("%s.json has no SessionStart hook running %s" % (role, BANNER))
        print("%s.json: %d deny rules, %d required, banner hook %s"
              % (role, len(deny), len(set(required)),
                 "present" if has_banner_hook(cfg) else "MISSING"))
    return problems


def main():
    root = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
    config_dir = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else os.path.join(root, "config", "claude")
    problems = check(config_dir)
    for p in problems:
        print("FAIL " + p)
    print("deny lists: %s" % ("FAIL" if problems else "PASS"))
    return 1 if problems else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

# The similarity audit

This repository says its firmware was written clean-room, without the FM-1's
GPL community firmwares (CONTRIBUTING.md). The audit backs that up with a
measurement. On every push to main, a CI job compares our firmware with
every FM-1 firmware repository it can find, and with an unrelated control
project, and puts the scores in the commit's record. Requirements:
R-AUDIT-1 to R-AUDIT-6 (docs/REQUIREMENTS.md).

Nobody working on this repository reads the targets. The spec side found
them from repository metadata alone. The job fetches them only inside CI,
and its logs and outputs hold scores and file names, never code. When the
job flags a pair, only an **auditor** may look (below).

## What is compared

- **Ours:** the C files under `firmware/` (`.c`, `.h`, and C++ suffixes if
  we ever have any). Assembly (`.S`) and linker scripts (`.ld`) are not
  compared: JPlag's C front end doesn't read them. `vendor/` is not ours
  and is never compared.
- **Base code:** the vendored JieLi SDK headers
  (`vendor/jieli-sdk/include_lib`). JPlag drops matches with base code, so
  code that both sides took from the SDK doesn't count against us.
- **Targets:** the C and C++ files of every target (below), at its pinned
  commit. `audit/targets.json` lists the targets; `paths` limits a target
  to some of its folders.
- **The control:** the C files of `raspberrypi/pico-examples` at tag
  `sdk-2.2.0`, commit `4c3a3dc0196dd426fddd709616d0da984e027bab`
  (BSD-3-Clause; `audit/audit.json`).

## The targets, from metadata only

`tools/audit-discover.py` builds `audit/targets.json` from
`audit/discover.json`. It asks GitHub's REST API, and `git ls-remote`, for
repository names, owners, descriptions, licences, languages, fork lists and
commit and tree SHAs. It never opens a target's files, README or web pages,
and never prints a description. A target is:

- **a seed:** Felucca (`hugelton/Felucca`), dinghy (`zvenson/dinghy`), the
  `fm1-sid/` and `probes/` folders of fm1-emu
  (`joakimeriksson/fm1-emu`), M-VAVE's `m-vave/fm1_open`, and the other
  FM-1 repositories of Felucca's author (`felucca-bsp`,
  `Felucca-Engines`, `Felucca-WebApp`, `felucca-mirror`);
- **a search hit:** a repository that one of the search queries finds and
  whose description names the FM-1, Felucca, GHOULBOX or Hortator. A
  repository that only matches by name must also be written in C or C++.
  "M-VAVE" or "dinghy" alone don't count, because they also name other
  products, boats and tools. dinghy's own lineage is found through its
  fork tree, and through descriptions that name the FM-1;
- **any fork of a target, to any depth.** A fork inherits its parent's
  `paths` and licence override.

The owner chose this wide net on 2026-10-22: every FM-1 repository, not
only Felucca's and dinghy's lineage. A target that turns out to be
unrelated costs only CI minutes. A target that is missed weakens the
claim.

Each target is **pinned** at its default branch's head commit, together
with that commit's tree. The job checks both. Targets whose tree (and
`paths`) is already in the list are marked `duplicate` and not fetched
again. Seeds come first, then other repositories, then forks, so a fork
that changed nothing is covered by the repository it copies. Empty
repositories are listed as `empty`.

Each target's **licence** is classed from its metadata as `gpl` (GPL,
LGPL, AGPL), `permissive` (MIT, BSD, Apache-2.0, ISC, WTFPL, CC0 and
similar), `other` (MPL-2.0, NOASSERTION, anything else) or `none` (no
licence). fm1-emu's metadata says MIT, but `fm1-sid/` is a GPL firmware
(docs/EXPOSURE.md), so that seed is classed `gpl`. The report shows each
target's class beside its scores. A flagged pair fails the job whatever
the licence.

**Unresolved:** *Felucca Salt* and *Felucca 8 Patterns*, both named in
CONTRIBUTING.md's forbidden list. No repository for either was found from
metadata on 2026-10-22; they may be distributed only as binaries. They are
listed in `discover.json` and in every report, and the owner adds a URL if
one turns up.

**Limits:** only the default branch is pinned; work on other branches,
and code in git submodules, is not fetched. A repository that neither
search finds nor any target's fork tree reaches is missed. Repositories
deleted after pinning are reported as `not fetched`.

### Rediscovery

`.github/workflows/audit-discover.yml` runs on the first day of every month,
and on demand. It runs `tools/audit-discover.py --write`, which uses
metadata only, as above. If any target is new, gone or has moved to a new
commit, it opens a pull request that changes `audit/targets.json` and lists
those repositories by name. It never fetches a target's code: only the
audit job does that.

Two things about that pull request:
- The repository setting "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull
  requests" must be on.
- GitHub does not run CI for a pull request that a workflow opens. The owner
  closes and reopens it to start `ci`, then merges it as usual.

## The method

JPlag 6.3.0 (the jar with dependencies, checked against its SHA-256 in
`audit/audit.json`) runs in the Java 25 image `eclipse-temurin`, pinned by
digest, with no network. Its settings:
- the C language module, with JPlag's default minimum match of 12 tokens;
- **every file is its own submission**, because JPlag drops a whole
  submission when one of its files fails to parse;
- our files and the control's files are the "new" submissions, and the
  target files are the "old" ones. JPlag compares every new file with every
  old one, and never compares two old ones;
- each target file is scored **once per blob**: forks share most files, and
  a report lists every target and path that holds a flagged blob;
- comparisons with no match at all are not written (`-m 0.000001`), which
  loses no score.

Each file pair gets three numbers:
- the **longest match**: the longest run of tokens the two files share;
- **max**: the matched tokens over the smaller file's tokens;
- **avg**: the matched tokens over the mean of the two files' tokens.

JPlag compares token structure, not names, so renaming identifiers does
not hide a copy.

### Why the longest match, not the ratio

Before choosing, the spec side scored the control against an unrelated
permissive embedded project: TinyUSB's `src/` at commit
`3fa7b06d284c0ac1d1078a0a2d09dceb405499e7` (MIT), 244 control files against
190 TinyUSB files, 27,492 file pairs, with the same settings. Nothing
GPL was involved.

| Score | Median | 99th percentile | 99.9th percentile | Highest |
|-------|--------|-----------------|-------------------|---------|
| Longest match (tokens) | 0 | 13 | 17 | 33 |
| max (ratio) | 0 | 0.116 | 0.325 | 0.857 |

The ratio reaches 0.857 between two unrelated projects: a short file is
easily "mostly matched" by chance. The longest match stays short between
unrelated code, while a copied function gives one long run. So the gate
uses the longest match, and the report shows `max` and `avg` beside it.

### The threshold

The job **fails** when a pair of one of our files and a target file has a
longest match above the **threshold**:

> threshold = the control's longest match with any target + 24 tokens

The control's highest score is what chance gives, in this run, against
these targets. That covers code idioms, common libraries and headers the
targets share with any embedded C. The margin of 24 tokens is twice
JPlag's minimum match: three or four C statements of identical structure,
beyond the longest run that unrelated embedded code shares with any
target. The calibration's highest chance run was 33 tokens, so the
threshold works out at about 55 to 60 tokens: six to eight lines of the
same code, which chance did not produce once in 27,492 pairs.

A second check fails if the control's own longest match with any target
exceeds **100 tokens** (C-AUDIT-CONTROL). That would mean the control is
not unrelated to some target (a target that copied pico-examples, say).
The baseline is then not trusted until the owner has looked at the names in
the report and chosen.

### What the gate cannot see

- **Small files.** A pair can fail only if its longest match is above the
  threshold. A verbatim copy of a file shorter than the threshold therefore
  can't fail the job. Today our files are 54, 20 and 16 tokens long, so an
  exact copy of one of them would show as a top pair with `max` 1.0 but
  would not fail the job. The report lists each of our files' token counts,
  and its top pairs with `max`, so a reader can see this. The gate gets
  stronger as the firmware grows.
- **Drift.** The control is fixed and the firmware grows. Larger files have
  more chances to share a run by accident. The control's score, measured
  against the same targets in the same run, is the yardstick. If the
  firmware ever dwarfs the control, a larger control is chosen, by pull
  request.
- **Reordered or rewritten code** splits a copied run into shorter ones.
  Clean-room work is meant to prevent that kind of derivation, and the audit
  is evidence for it, not proof.

### Why this control

`raspberrypi/pico-examples` is:
- permissive (BSD-3-Clause);
- pinned at a release tag;
- embedded C of the same kind as ours: startup and clocks, timers,
  interrupts, UART, GPIO, DMA, audio and display examples;
- mostly small files, as ours are.

It is written for a different chip family (RP2040 and RP2350) and has
nothing to do with the FM-1, so its similarity to the targets is chance
and shared idiom, not copying. Its scores measure the noise floor that ours
are judged against. TinyUSB, used for the calibration above, was not chosen
as the control: an FM-1 firmware could reasonably vendor TinyUSB for USB
MIDI, which would raise the baseline.

## Running it

`.github/workflows/audit.yml`:
- runs on every push to main, and on demand (`workflow_dispatch`, with a
  choice of set);
- never runs for pull requests: there is no such trigger, and both jobs
  also require main.

GitHub offers the on-demand run only once the workflow file is on main, so
its first run is the push that merges it.

- **Sets.** `full` scores every target that isn't a duplicate. `fast`
  scores the four seeds Felucca, dinghy, fm1-emu's `fm1-sid/` (with
  `probes/`) and `fm1_open`. Pushes to main run `full`. If a full run ever
  takes more than about 30 minutes, push runs switch to `fast` and a nightly
  schedule runs `full`. That is one change to `audit.yml`'s triggers, by
  pull request, and this page then says so.
- **Self-test first.** Each run starts with `tools/audit.py selftest`. It
  builds a made-up local target that holds verbatim copies of our files,
  runs the whole pipeline on it, and checks that each of our files is found
  and that the leak check passes (C-AUDIT-SELFTEST). No GPL code is
  involved.
- **Job `audit`** has read-only permissions, no environment and no
  secrets. For each target in turn it:
  1. fetches the pinned commit into a temporary folder: depth 1, blob-less,
     with a sparse checkout of the C and C++ files only;
  2. checks the commit's tree against the pin;
  3. copies each file it hasn't seen before into the pool;
  4. deletes the checkout.

  Then it runs JPlag once over the whole pool. JPlag's console output goes

# The similarity audit

This repository says its firmware was written clean-room, without the FM-1's
GPL community firmwares (CONTRIBUTING.md). The audit backs that up with a
measurement. On every push to main, a CI job compares our firmware with
every FM-1 firmware repository it can find, and with an unrelated control
project, and puts the scores in the commit's record. Requirements:
R-AUDIT-1 to R-AUDIT-6 (docs/REQUIREMENTS.md).

Nobody working on this repository reads the targets. The spec side found
them from repository metadata alone. The job fetches them only inside CI,
and its logs and outputs hold scores and file names, never code. When the
job flags a pair, only an **auditor** may look (below).

## What is compared

- **Ours:** the C files under `firmware/` (`.c`, `.h`, and C++ suffixes if
  we ever have any). Assembly (`.S`) and linker scripts (`.ld`) are not
  compared: JPlag's C front end doesn't read them. `vendor/` is not ours
  and is never compared.
- **Base code:** the vendored JieLi SDK headers
  (`vendor/jieli-sdk/include_lib`). JPlag drops matches with base code, so
  code that both sides took from the SDK doesn't count against us.
- **Targets:** the C and C++ files of every target (below), at its pinned
  commit. `audit/targets.json` lists the targets; `paths` limits a target
  to some of its folders.
- **The control:** the C files of `raspberrypi/pico-examples` at tag
  `sdk-2.2.0`, commit `4c3a3dc0196dd426fddd709616d0da984e027bab`
  (BSD-3-Clause; `audit/audit.json`).

## The targets, from metadata only

`tools/audit-discover.py` builds `audit/targets.json` from
`audit/discover.json`. It asks GitHub's REST API, and `git ls-remote`, for
repository names, owners, descriptions, licences, languages, fork lists and
commit and tree SHAs. It never opens a target's files, README or web pages,
and never prints a description. A target is:

- **a seed:** Felucca (`hugelton/Felucca`), dinghy (`zvenson/dinghy`), the
  `fm1-sid/` and `probes/` folders of fm1-emu
  (`joakimeriksson/fm1-emu`), M-VAVE's `m-vave/fm1_open`, and the other
  FM-1 repositories of Felucca's author (`felucca-bsp`,
  `Felucca-Engines`, `Felucca-WebApp`, `felucca-mirror`);
- **a search hit:** a repository that one of the search queries finds and
  whose description names the FM-1, Felucca, GHOULBOX or Hortator. A
  repository that only matches by name must also be written in C or C++.
  "M-VAVE" or "dinghy" alone don't count, because they also name other
  products, boats and tools. dinghy's own lineage is found through its
  fork tree, and through descriptions that name the FM-1;
- **any fork of a target, to any depth.** A fork inherits its parent's
  `paths` and licence override.

The owner chose this wide net on 2026-10-22: every FM-1 repository, not
only Felucca's and dinghy's lineage. A target that turns out to be
unrelated costs only CI minutes. A target that is missed weakens the
claim.

Each target is **pinned** at its default branch's head commit, together
with that commit's tree. The job checks both. Targets whose tree (and
`paths`) is already in the list are marked `duplicate` and not fetched
again. Seeds come first, then other repositories, then forks, so a fork
that changed nothing is covered by the repository it copies. Empty
repositories are listed as `empty`.

Each target's **licence** is classed from its metadata as `gpl` (GPL,
LGPL, AGPL), `permissive` (MIT, BSD, Apache-2.0, ISC, WTFPL, CC0 and
similar), `other` (MPL-2.0, NOASSERTION, anything else) or `none` (no
licence). fm1-emu's metadata says MIT, but `fm1-sid/` is a GPL firmware
(docs/EXPOSURE.md), so that seed is classed `gpl`. The report shows each
target's class beside its scores. A flagged pair fails the job whatever
the licence.

**Unresolved:** *Felucca Salt* and *Felucca 8 Patterns*, both named in
CONTRIBUTING.md's forbidden list. No repository for either was found from
metadata on 2026-10-22; they may be distributed only as binaries. They are
listed in `discover.json` and in every report, and the owner adds a URL if
one turns up.

**Limits:** only the default branch is pinned; work on other branches,
and code in git submodules, is not fetched. A repository that neither
search finds nor any target's fork tree reaches is missed. Repositories
deleted after pinning are reported as `not fetched`.

### Rediscovery

`.github/workflows/audit-discover.yml` runs on the first day of every month,
and on demand. It runs `tools/audit-discover.py --write`, which uses
metadata only, as above. If any target is new, gone or has moved to a new
commit, it opens a pull request that changes `audit/targets.json` and lists
those repositories by name. It never fetches a target's code: only the
audit job does that.

Two things about that pull request:
- The repository setting "Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull
  requests" must be on.
- GitHub does not run CI for a pull request that a workflow opens. The owner
  closes and reopens it to start `ci`, then merges it as usual.

## The method

JPlag 6.3.0 (the jar with dependencies, checked against its SHA-256 in
`audit/audit.json`) runs in the Java 25 image `eclipse-temurin`, pinned by
digest, with no network. Its settings:
- the C language module, with JPlag's default minimum match of 12 tokens;
- **every file is its own submission**, because JPlag drops a whole
  submission when one of its files fails to parse;
- our files and the control's files are the "new" submissions, and the
  target files are the "old" ones. JPlag compares every new file with every
  old one, and never compares two old ones;
- each target file is scored **once per blob**: forks share most files, and
  a report lists every target and path that holds a flagged blob;
- comparisons with no match at all are not written (`-m 0.000001`), which
  loses no score.

Each file pair gets three numbers:
- the **longest match**: the longest run of tokens the two files share;
- **max**: the matched tokens over the smaller file's tokens;
- **avg**: the matched tokens over the mean of the two files' tokens.

JPlag compares token structure, not names, so renaming identifiers does
not hide a copy.

### Why the longest match, not the ratio

Before choosing, the spec side scored the control against an unrelated
permissive embedded project: TinyUSB's `src/` at commit
`3fa7b06d284c0ac1d1078a0a2d09dceb405499e7` (MIT), 244 control files against
190 TinyUSB files, 27,492 file pairs, with the same settings. Nothing
GPL was involved.

| Score | Median | 99th percentile | 99.9th percentile | Highest |
|-------|--------|-----------------|-------------------|---------|
| Longest match (tokens) | 0 | 13 | 17 | 33 |
| max (ratio) | 0 | 0.116 | 0.325 | 0.857 |

The ratio reaches 0.857 between two unrelated projects: a short file is
easily "mostly matched" by chance. The longest match stays short between
unrelated code, while a copied function gives one long run. So the gate
uses the longest match, and the report shows `max` and `avg` beside it.

### The threshold

The job **fails** when a pair of one of our files and a target file has a
longest match above the **threshold**:

> threshold = the control's longest match with any target + 24 tokens

The control's highest score is what chance gives, in this run, against
these targets. That covers code idioms, common libraries and headers the
targets share with any embedded C. The margin of 24 tokens is twice
JPlag's minimum match: three or four C statements of identical structure,
beyond the longest run that unrelated embedded code shares with any
target. The calibration's highest chance run was 33 tokens, so the
threshold works out at about 55 to 60 tokens: six to eight lines of the
same code, which chance did not produce once in 27,492 pairs.

A second check fails if the control's own longest match with any target
exceeds **100 tokens** (C-AUDIT-CONTROL). That would mean the control is
not unrelated to some target (a target that copied pico-examples, say).
The baseline is then not trusted until the owner has looked at the names in
the report and chosen.

### What the gate cannot see

- **Small files.** A pair can fail only if its longest match is above the
  threshold. A verbatim copy of a file shorter than the threshold therefore
  can't fail the job. Today our files are 54, 20 and 16 tokens long, so an
  exact copy of one of them would show as a top pair with `max` 1.0 but
  would not fail the job. The report lists each of our files' token counts,
  and its top pairs with `max`, so a reader can see this. The gate gets
  stronger as the firmware grows.
- **Drift.** The control is fixed and the firmware grows. Larger files have
  more chances to share a run by accident. The control's score, measured
  against the same targets in the same run, is the yardstick. If the
  firmware ever dwarfs the control, a larger control is chosen, by pull
  request.
- **Reordered or rewritten code** splits a copied run into shorter ones.
  Clean-room work is meant to prevent that kind of derivation, and the audit
  is evidence for it, not proof.

### Why this control

`raspberrypi/pico-examples` is:
- permissive (BSD-3-Clause);
- pinned at a release tag;
- embedded C of the same kind as ours: startup and clocks, timers,
  interrupts, UART, GPIO, DMA, audio and display examples;
- mostly small files, as ours are.

It is written for a different chip family (RP2040 and RP2350) and has
nothing to do with the FM-1, so its similarity to the targets is chance
and shared idiom, not copying. Its scores measure the noise floor that ours
are judged against. TinyUSB, used for the calibration above, was not chosen
as the control: an FM-1 firmware could reasonably vendor TinyUSB for USB
MIDI, which would raise the baseline.

## Running it

`.github/workflows/audit.yml`:
- runs on every push to main, and on demand (`workflow_dispatch`, with a
  choice of set);
- never runs for pull requests: there is no such trigger, and both jobs
  also require main.

GitHub offers the on-demand run only once the workflow file is on main, so
its first run is the push that merges it.

- **Sets.** `full` scores every target that isn't a duplicate. `fast`
  scores the four seeds Felucca, dinghy, fm1-emu's `fm1-sid/` (with
  `probes/`) and `fm1_open`. Pushes to main run `full`. If a full run ever
  takes more than about 30 minutes, push runs switch to `fast` and a nightly
  schedule runs `full`. That is one change to `audit.yml`'s triggers, by
  pull request, and this page then says so.
- **Self-test first.** Each run starts with `tools/audit.py selftest`. It
  builds a made-up local target that holds verbatim copies of our files,
  runs the whole pipeline on it, and checks that each of our files is found
  and that the leak check passes (C-AUDIT-SELFTEST). No GPL code is
  involved.
- **Job `audit`** has read-only permissions, no environment and no
  secrets. For each target in turn it:
  1. fetches the pinned commit into a temporary folder: depth 1, blob-less,

  checks, saying the leak check failed.

  1. downloads the artifact;
  2. checks that it holds only that report (`tools/audit.py

`audit/audit.json`) runs in the Java 25 image `eclipse-temurin`, pinned by
digest, with no network. Its settings:
- the C language module, with JPlag's default minimum match of 12 tokens;
- **every file is its own submission**, because JPlag drops a whole
  submission when one of its files fails to parse;
- our files and the control's files are the "new" submissions, and the
  target files are the "old" ones. JPlag compares every new file with every
  old one, and never compares two old ones;
- each target file is scored **once per blob**: forks share most files, and
  a report lists every target and path that holds a flagged blob;
- comparisons with no match at all are not written (`-m 0.000001`), which
  loses no score.

Each file pair gets three numbers:
- the **longest match**: the longest run of tokens the two files share;
- **max**: the matched tokens over the smaller file's tokens;
- **avg**: the matched tokens over the mean of the two files' tokens.

JPlag compares token structure, not names, so renaming identifiers does
not hide a copy.

### Why the longest match, not the ratio

Before choosing, the spec side scored the control against an unrelated
permissive embedded project: TinyUSB's `src/` at commit
`3fa7b06d284c0ac1d1078a0a2d09dceb405499e7` (MIT), 244 control files against
190 TinyUSB files, 27,492 file pairs, with the same settings. Nothing
GPL was involved.

| Score | Median | 99th percentile | 99.9th percentile | Highest |
|-------|--------|-----------------|-------------------|---------|
| Longest match (tokens) | 0 | 13 | 17 | 33 |
| max (ratio) | 0 | 0.116 | 0.325 | 0.857 |

The ratio reaches 0.857 between two unrelated projects: a short file is
easily "mostly matched" by chance. The longest match stays short between
unrelated code, while a copied function gives one long run. So the gate
uses the longest match, and the report shows `max` and `avg` beside it.

### The threshold

The job **fails** when a pair of one of our files and a target file has a
longest match above the **threshold**:

> threshold = the control's longest match with any target + 24 tokens

The control's highest score is what chance gives, in this run, against
these targets. That covers code idioms, common libraries and headers the
targets share with any embedded C. The margin of 24 tokens is twice
JPlag's minimum match: three or four C statements of identical structure,
beyond the longest run that unrelated embedded code shares with any
target. The calibration's highest chance run was 33 tokens, so the
threshold works out at about 55 to 60 tokens: six to eight lines of the
same code, which chance did not produce once in 27,492 pairs.

A second check fails if the control's own longest match with any target
exceeds **100 tokens** (C-AUDIT-CONTROL). That would mean the control is
not unrelated to some target (a target that copied pico-examples, say).
The baseline is then not trusted until the owner has looked at the names in
the report and chosen.

### What the gate cannot see

- **Small files.** A pair can fail only if its longest match is above the
  threshold. A verbatim copy of a file shorter than the threshold therefore
  can't fail the job. Today our files are 54, 20 and 16 tokens long, so an
  exact copy of one of them would show as a top pair with `max` 1.0 but
  would not fail the job. The report lists each of our files' token counts,
  and its top pairs with `max`, so a reader can see this. The gate gets
  stronger as the firmware grows.
- **Drift.** The control is fixed and the firmware grows. Larger files have
  more chances to share a run by accident. The control's score, measured
  against the same targets in the same run, is the yardstick. If the
  firmware ever dwarfs the control, a larger control is chosen, by pull
  request.
- **Reordered or rewritten code** splits a copied run into shorter ones.
  Clean-room work is meant to prevent that kind of derivation, and the audit
  is evidence for it, not proof.

### Why this control

`raspberrypi/pico-examples` is:
- permissive (BSD-3-Clause);
- pinned at a release tag;
- embedded C of the same kind as ours: startup and clocks, timers,
  interrupts, UART, GPIO, DMA, audio and display examples;
- mostly small files, as ours are.

It is written for a different chip family (RP2040 and RP2350) and has
nothing to do with the FM-1, so its similarity to the targets is chance
and shared idiom, not copying. Its scores measure the noise floor that ours
are judged against. TinyUSB, used for the calibration above, was not chosen
as the control: an FM-1 firmware could reasonably vendor TinyUSB for USB
MIDI, which would raise the baseline.

## Running it

`.github/workflows/audit.yml`:
- runs on every push to main, and on demand (`workflow_dispatch`, with a
  choice of set);
- never runs for pull requests: there is no such trigger, and both jobs
  also require main.

GitHub offers the on-demand run only once the workflow file is on main, so
its first run is the push that merges it.

- **Sets.** `full` scores every target that isn't a duplicate. `fast`
  scores the four seeds Felucca, dinghy, fm1-emu's `fm1-sid/` (with
  `probes/`) and `fm1_open`. Pushes to main run `full`. If a full run ever
  takes more than about 30 minutes, push runs switch to `fast` and a nightly
  schedule runs `full`. That is one change to `audit.yml`'s triggers, by
  pull request, and this page then says so.
- **Self-test first.** Each run starts with `tools/audit.py selftest`. It
  builds a made-up local target that holds verbatim copies of our files,
  runs the whole pipeline on it, and checks that each of our files is found
  and that the leak check passes (C-AUDIT-SELFTEST). No GPL code is
  involved.
- **Job `audit`** has read-only permissions, no environment and no
  secrets. For each target in turn it:
  1. fetches the pinned commit into a temporary folder: depth 1, blob-less,
     with a sparse checkout of the C and C++ files only;
  2. checks the commit's tree against the pin;
  3. copies each file it hasn't seen before into the pool;
  4. deletes the checkout.

  Then it runs JPlag once over the whole pool. JPlag's console output goes
  to a log in the temporary folder that is never shown, because a parse
  error quotes source. Its report archive embeds the files it compared, so
  the tool reads only three JSON members of it (comparisons, failed files,
  token counts: names and numbers), then deletes it. The temporary folder
  is removed whatever happens, and the job says so. Nothing is cached. The
  only artifact is `report.json` and `report.md`.
- **The leak check (C-AUDIT-LEAK).** Before the report is written, every
  line of every target file that is 24 characters or longer (after
  trimming) is looked for in it. On a hit the report is cut down to its
  checks, saying the leak check failed.
- **Job `record`** never sees a target. It:
  1. downloads the artifact;
  2. checks that it holds only that report (`tools/audit.py
     check-artifact`);
  3. appends it to the commit's record on the `records` branch, at
     `records/<sha>/audit/<run>-<attempt>/`, with the `records`
     environment's deploy key.

  If the records workflow is pushing at the same moment, it starts again
  from the branch's tip.

### The report

`report.json` and `report.md` hold:
- the pinned JPlag, Java image and control, the control's highest longest
  match, the threshold and the margin;
- the checks (C-AUDIT-JPLAG, -PIN, -CONTROL, -SCORE, -LEAK) and their
  traceability to R-AUDIT-*;
- **our top 20 file pairs**: our file, the target repositories and paths
  holding the matched file (the first ten of them, and how many there are),
  each with its licence class, and the longest match, max and avg;
- the control's top five pairs, and its best pair with our own files;
- each of our files' token counts;
- every target: its pinned commit, licence class, files fetched (and how
  many were new to the pool), our longest and the control's longest match
  with it, and how many of its files JPlag could not parse or found too
  small;
- the flagged pairs, every place listed; pairs accepted by an auditor's
  finding; how many targets were skipped as duplicates or empty; and the
  unresolved names.

## When the audit fails

Nobody on the spec side or the firmware side opens the matched code, or the
target, to see what matched.

1. **The owner is told.** The failed `audit` run and its report say which
   of our files, which target files (by name) and what scores. Whoever
   sees it first tells the owner, and repeats nothing beyond those names
   and numbers.
2. **The owner starts an auditor session** (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Roles"):
   - in a folder of its own, set up with `tools/auditor-setup.sh
     ~/<top>/auditor`, which installs `config/claude/auditor.json`;
   - it adds its entry to docs/EXPOSURE.md before anything else;
   - the auditor reads only the flagged pairs: our file, and the target
     file at its pinned commit.
3. **The auditor writes a finding** in `audit/findings/`, in general terms
   only: which of our files, the target's repository and path, the scores,
   and the conclusion. Possible conclusions are coincidence, a common
   source (the SDK, a datasheet's sequence, a standard idiom), or derived.
   It contains no target code and no description of the target's
   structure. The finding comes by pull request, reviewed by the owner.
4. **Then:**
   - *Coincidence or a common source:* the pair goes in
     `audit/accepted.json`, with our file, the target's repository and path,
     the accepted longest match and the finding. A higher score later fails
     again.
   - *Derived:* the owner decides how the firmware side replaces our file
     clean-room, from HARDWARE-SPEC.md, without the finding's details.
5. **The auditor is done for good.** It never writes firmware or spec
   afterwards, in any session.

**Auditor transcripts are never archived in this repository**, because they
hold GPL source. The owner's decision of 2026-10-22:
- each one goes to a separate private repository owned by the owner
  (`small-beeps-audit`), committed there with an OpenTimestamps proof;
- that repository is created only when the first auditor session runs, and
  only with the owner's approval;
- here, docs/EXPOSURE.md records the auditor session's ID, the transcript's
  SHA-256 and the private repository's commit;
- `tools/check-transcripts.py` fails on any transcript outside
  `sessions/clean/` and `sessions/spec/`, so an auditor transcript put here
  by mistake fails CI.

## Files

| File | What it is |
|------|------------|
| `audit/discover.json` | Seeds, search queries, the mention rule, unresolved names. |
| `audit/targets.json` | Every target, pinned: commit, tree, licence class, status. Written by `tools/audit-discover.py`. |
| `audit/audit.json` | JPlag and the Java image (pinned), the control (pinned), base code, the margin, the ceiling, the fast set. |
| `audit/accepted.json` | Pairs accepted by an auditor's finding. |
| `audit/findings/` | Auditors' findings (none yet). |
| `tools/audit.py` | The audit, its self-test, and the artifact check. |
| `tools/audit-discover.py` | Finds the targets from metadata. |
| `.github/workflows/audit.yml` | The audit and its record. |
| `.github/workflows/audit-discover.yml` | The monthly rediscovery. |
| `config/claude/auditor.json` | The auditor's Claude Code settings. |

"""Checks commit messages against .gitmessage (R-PROC-1, check C-COMMIT-MSG).

  check-commit-msg.py --file MSGFILE     one message (the commit-msg hook;
                                         lines starting with # are removed)
  check-commit-msg.py --range A..B       every commit in A..B
  check-commit-msg.py --range ..B        every commit reachable from B
  check-commit-msg.py --commit SHA       one commit

Merge commits are exempt (their pull request carries the sections) and are
listed as such. Exit status 1 if any message fails.
"""
import argparse
import re
import subprocess
import sys

FIELDS = ["What", "Why", "How", "Result", "Sources", "Exposure"]
SUBJECT_RE = re.compile(r"^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9/_.-]*: \S.*$")
FIELD_RE = re.compile(r"^(%s):(.*)$" % "|".join(FIELDS))
TRAILER_RE = re.compile(r"^([A-Za-z][A-Za-z-]*): (.+)$")
KNOWN_TRAILERS = ("Model", "Claude-Session", "Co-Authored-By", "Signed-off-by")
MAX_SUBJECT = 100


def strip_comments(text):
    return "\n".join(l for l in text.splitlines() if not l.startswith("#"))


def validate(message, author=""):
    """Returns a list of problems; empty means the message is fine."""
    problems = []
    lines = message.strip("\n").splitlines()
    if not lines:
        return ["empty message"]
    subject = lines[0]
    if not SUBJECT_RE.match(subject):
        problems.append("subject must look like '<area>: <what changed>' "
                        "with a lower-case area: %r" % subject)
    if len(subject) > MAX_SUBJECT:
        problems.append("subject longer than %d characters" % MAX_SUBJECT)
    if len(lines) < 2 or lines[1].strip():
        problems.append("line 2 must be empty")

    values = {}
    order = []
    current = None
    trailers = {}
    for line in lines[2:]:
        m = FIELD_RE.match(line)
        if m:
            current = m.group(1)
            if current in values:
                problems.append("field %s: appears twice" % current)
            order.append(current)
            values[current] = m.group(2).strip()
            continue
        if current and (line.startswith(" ") or line.startswith("\t")):
